cohort: The participants included non-pregnant women, normal pregnant women at 20-34 gestational weeks and 34-41 gestational weeks, and women diagnosed with early-onset or late-onset preeclampsia.
finding: Circulating miR-31 levels were significantly down-regulated in early-onset preeclampsia, while miR-21 levels were significantly lower in late-onset preeclampsia, suggesting their potential as diagnostic biomarkers.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at non-pregnancy, 20-34 gestational weeks, and 34-41 gestational weeks, as well as at the time of preeclampsia diagnosis.
gest_age: 20-34 gestational weeks (normal pregnancy, EOPE) and 34-41 gestational weeks (normal pregnancy, LOPE)
